seoTitle: Free Color Names Lookup: Nearest CSS Colour Name
metaDescription: Find the nearest named CSS colour for any HEX, RGB or HSL value, or search colour names by text. Free, runs in your browser, nothing is uploaded.
intro: Takes colours or name fragments, one per line. For a colour value it lists the closest CSS named colours by perceptual distance. For text it lists names that contain it.
why:
You have a hex code and want a friendly name for a design token, a comment or a colour-blind-friendly note. Or you remember part of a name, such as "slate" or "sky", and want to see what is available and what hex it maps to.

Paste several lines at once. A line that parses as a colour returns the nearest named CSS colours, ranked by distance in the perceptual OKLab space, so the match reflects how colours look rather than how close the numbers are. A line that does not parse is treated as a search term and returns every name containing it, with its hex code. Only the standard CSS colour names are included. The lookup runs in your browser and nothing is uploaded.
howTo: Enter a colour value or part of a colour name on each line.
Read the ranked nearest names, or the matching names, in the output.
Note the hex codes and distances.

faq.a: The standard CSS named colours such as tomato, steelblue and rebeccapurple. It does not include marketing names, such as paint or brand colour names, from outside the CSS list.
It is the Euclidean distance between two colours in the OKLab space. A smaller number is a closer match, and a distance near zero means the named colour is practically identical.

faq.q: How does it decide between colour and search?
faq.a: It first tries to read the line as a colour. If that fails, for example for the text "sky", it treats it as a search term and ignores case and spaces.

faq.q: Which colour formats can I enter?
faq.a: Hex codes, rgb, hsl and similar CSS functions, and existing colour names. Each line is handled separately, so you can mix formats in one go.
